# Who can become root through your sudoers file?

> Paste /etc/sudoers and the files in /etc/sudoers.d: find NOPASSWD ALL, editors, pagers, shells, interpreters and find/tar/systemctl/docker rules that give a root shell, ALL minus su, commands in user-writable directories, wildcard arguments, SETENV, env_keep LD_PRELOAD, !env_reset, NOPASSWD rules a later rule overrides, and sudoers.d files sudo skips because their names contain a dot. Each finding has its file, line and fix, and the report lists who can become root and how. Free, runs in your browser, nothing uploaded.

Free to use and source available (FSL-1.1-MIT). A static read of the files you give it, not a security audit and not visudo -c; a clean result is not proof a system is safe. The parser's reading of 41 grammar test cases matches sudo 1.9.15p5's own cvtsudoers. Which programs offer shell escapes is a long-known list documented in detail by GTFOBins; the tool is not affiliated with it or with the sudo project.

## Pages

- [The tool](https://marisstella.app/sudoers-check/)
- [sudoers mistakes explained: what each one hands out and the fix](https://marisstella.app/sudoers-check/sudoers-mistakes-explained.html)

## CLI

- `sudo node check.mjs /etc/` reads /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d/* with include order resolved and prints file:line findings and who can become root; `--format json`, `--fail-on-risk` (exit 2 on high or medium). Node 18+, no dependencies.

## Source

- [Source code and README](https://github.com/duncan-haywood/oss-monorepo/tree/main/ventures/sudoers-check): FSL-1.1-MIT licensed.
